issues.legal_issue: The constitutional requirement that compulsory acquisition serve a public purpose did not render the existing acquisition statute, including its provisions for company acquisitions, redundant or invalid.
material_facts: The land was acquired under an enactment that predated the Constitution.
The challenge argued that the constitutional restriction on compulsory acquisition had made the statute’s provisions for company acquisitions redundant or invalid.
issues.conclusion: The existing enactment, including its company-acquisition provisions, was saved from attack under the constitutional acquisition provision and was not rendered redundant or invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31(5)(a) saved an existing law of this kind from the operation of Article 31(2). The Court relied on Babu Barkaya Thakur v. State of Bombay, which held that the Land Acquisition Act was immune from an Article 31(2) challenge by virtue of Article 31(5)(a).

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_compulsory_a: A person challenged a compulsory acquisition on the ground that the constitutional public-purpose requirement invalidated the governing law.
predicates.acquisition_under_existing_law: The acquisition proceeded under a law that was already in force when the Constitution came into effect.

issues.definition: When a compulsory acquisition under an existing law is challenged on this constitutional ground, the existing law remains valid.

issues.legal_issue: Acquiring land to provide residential housing for industrial workers serves a public purpose.
material_facts: The land was acquired for a labour colony consisting of residential quarters for industrial workers.
The housing was part of a government-sponsored scheme, and the workers had organized themselves into a cooperative housing society.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition served a public purpose, even apart from the provision that expressly included government-sponsored labour colonies among specified purposes.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on Babu Barkaya Thakur v. State of Bombay for the principle that building residential quarters for industrial labour is a public purpose. It also noted that the relevant Punjab amendment expressly included construction of labour colonies under a government-sponsored housing scheme.

predicates.compulsory_land_acquisition: A public authority compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.housing_for_industrial_workers: The land was acquired to provide residential housing for industrial workers.

issues.definition: If land is compulsorily acquired to provide residential housing for industrial workers, the acquisition serves a public purpose.

issues.legal_issue: The procedure for acquisition for a company under the company-acquisition provisions is unnecessary when public funds bear part of the acquisition cost, but applies when the company bears the entire cost.
material_facts: The land was acquired for the benefit of a cooperative society that qualified as a company under the acquisition statute.
The government housing scheme provided for public funds to contribute to the cost of the land and structures through subsidies and loans.
The society or its members were to provide the remaining contribution.
issues.conclusion: Because public funds were to bear part of the compensation cost, the acquisition was not for the company alone and compliance with the company-acquisition procedure was unnecessary.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 6 and 39–41 of the Land Acquisition Act, read with Part VII, an acquisition for a company alone requires compliance with the company-acquisition procedure. An acquisition for a public purpose may be made where the cost is borne wholly or partly from public funds; an acquisition for a company for a public purpose is therefore outside that procedure when public funds contribute to its cost. The Court relied on Babu Barkaya Thakur v. State of Bombay concerning the distinction between public-purpose acquisitions and acquisitions for companies.

predicates.acquisition_for_company: The land was acquired for the benefit of a company or an entity treated as a company for acquisition purposes.
predicates.public_funds_cover_part_of_cost: Public funds were to bear some part of the cost of acquiring the land.

issues.definition: When land is acquired for a company and public funds bear part of the acquisition cost, the company-acquisition procedure is not required.
